findings.where: Title block / top bar, at both widths: the DRAWING 'MMM-GA-001' and SCALE 'NTS' cells beside the PROFILE, ARTICLES, BLOG and CONTACT nav cells (on the phone they share the logo's row, above the nav row)
findings.fault: The fixed cells and the nav links look the same: the same ruled cell, the same pale capitals on blue, the same height in one row. Nothing marks which cells take you somewhere, so the bar reads as six or seven equal links. The drawing number and the scale look clickable but do nothing.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor from a development bank looking for Mark's profile or contact details scans the top bar for links. They can't tell the four real links from the drawing labels, and clicking 'MMM-GA-001' does nothing. That is a small but real moment of 'is this broken?' on the first screen.

findings.where: Hero, 'WRITE TO MARK' (the one primary action), and the CONTACT nav item
findings.fault: The page's only way to get in touch is a mailto link, and Mark's address appears nowhere on the page. Without a mail program set up, or on a work machine where mailto opens nothing or opens the wrong account, the button does nothing the visitor can see. They have no address to copy, and CONTACT goes nowhere either (#).
findings.who_objects: Staff at multilateral banks and agencies often work in browser webmail or on locked-down machines. If the one action fails silently, they can't contact Mark, and the page exists to get that contact.

findings.where: Motion sketch, 'REPLAY THE CUT', compared with the article specimen's 'Streamlining the PPP Process…' link
findings.fault: One look, two functions. The replay button, which does something on this page, has the same treatment as the article link, which takes you to a PDF: bold pale text with an underline. Its capitals and letter spacing match the static section labels (PALETTE, MOTION SKETCH), not a button. The site's link look now also means 'run an action'.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who clicks the underlined replay text expects to leave the page, and is surprised when the drawing replays instead. Angélique and the layout round would carry the mixed signal on into every page built from this tile.

findings.where: Article specimen, the boxed lecture item ('Streamlining the PPP Process…', Lecture · 2026-04-23 · PDF)
findings.fault: The whole item has its own ruled box, the way a card the visitor can click would, but only the underlined title is a link. Clicking the box's empty right side or the 'Lecture · PDF' line does nothing.
findings.who_objects: A reader who sees a boxed item with a PDF label will click anywhere in the box to open the lecture, above all on a phone where the box spans the screen. Clicks that land outside the title do nothing.
